payload.blocks: Only the caller set of the widen verb and whether PS-24 is amended. The drift check and the planner-without-discussion task go on without this answer.
payload.headline: Who may call the new plan-widen door: the supervisor only, or also the plan's own lead with an answered owner question?

parts.cause: Your decision PS-24 (supervision spec) says a lead may not change its own footprint; the land door refuses it as footprint-change-refused. That rule guards against a lead silently widening itself. The new door can require your answered question as proof, which removes that risk, but letting the lead call it amends PS-24, so the choice is yours.

options.cost: The host route has to read the question store when the lead calls; about the same size as the verb itself.
options.does: The lead calls plan widen --approved-by <q-id>; the host checks the question is answered and its ref is this plan, then lands plan.md. The supervisor can still call it. A lead footprint change without a valid answered question stays refused.
options.gain: The widening happens the moment you answer: no supervisor wake, no hand edit, no 40-minute park.
options.harm: PS-24 is amended: the lead's footprint bound now rests on the question store's check rather than on a second session.
options.label: Lead too, with an answered question

options.cost: Smallest verb; the wait per widening stays.
options.does: Only the supervisor (and secretary) call plan widen. The lead keeps asking, and the supervisor applies the answer after its next wake.
options.gain: PS-24 stays exactly as decided; a second session always performs the change.
options.harm: Every widening still waits for a supervisor wake after your answer, as the two pending plans do today.
options.label: Supervisor only, PS-24 unchanged

parts.recommendation: Lead too, with an answered question: your answer is already the approval PS-24 wanted, and requiring it in the door keeps the guard while removing the hop that parks plans.

scope.allows: Setting the caller set of the plan widen verb and, for the first option, amending PS-24 so that a lead footprint change passes only with an answered owner question whose ref is its own plan.
scope.forbids: Any other change to PS-24 or to the lead's grant (it still writes only its plan directory), and any widening without an answered owner question.

parts.what: The discussion proposes one verb, plan widen, that turns an answered owner question into a landed footprint change, writing the frontmatter list and the phase row together. Today a lead that needs one more file asks you, you answer widen, then the supervisor must wake and hand-edit plan.md. Two plans sit like that right now (q-myvzcbz3sx, q-vqyxe5oi6j, answered 01:44Z, not yet applied).
